purpose: External geometry-validation fixture for canonical Asscher wireframe and facet-family extraction; not a quality label or training target.

source.thread_title: Why cut asschers with small corners and windmills?

classes.manual_reported: Reported by DiaGem/Yoram from direct/manual measurement or cutting knowledge; primary physical evidence for this fixture.
classes.photo_estimate: Estimated by Sergey from a supplied photograph; independent image-derived comparison target.
classes.scanner_reported: Instrument output quoted in the thread; context only because the participants explicitly question scanner accuracy for this stone.
classes.design_context: Intended/model geometry discussed around the cut; not finished-stone ground truth.
classes.source_media_unresolved: An original image is referenced in the thread, but exact source bytes are not yet archived.

evidence_policy.rule: Never silently promote photo estimates, scanner output, design values, or Sparkles inferences to manual ground truth.

crown_height_pct.note: Also reported by OGI in post 102; post 134 describes 23.9% as the actual crown height.

table_pct.note: DiaGem says the table went down to 27% due to step sizes. OGI is separately recorded as 27.1%.

p3_angles_deg.uncertainty_note: DiaGem says at least two P3 facets are 31 degrees and the other two are maybe 30 degrees, associated with creating the pointed culet.

relative_physical_facet_lengths.p1_vs_p2: approximately_equal; P1 may be fractionally longer

known_asymmetry.observation: Two opposed P3 facets were adjusted during final cutting to close the culet; north/south and west/east P3 therefore have a small angle difference.
Table junctions with C3 are slightly unbalanced because the very small table gave limited dop holding surface.

independent_photo_estimate.note: These are deliberately stored as an independent image-derived estimate, not as the physical ground truth.

projection_caveat.observation: P1 appears longer than P2 in the photograph even though DiaGem says their real physical lengths are practically identical.
projection_caveat.implication: Do not equate image-plane facet width/length with physical facet length without an explicit projection model.

positive.criterion: front light not very bright; avoid flashes
pavilion side facets should not be visible

negative_example.reason: Sergey says pavilion side facets are visible, indicating large tilt or short focal length, and therefore declines to estimate from that image.

scanner_context.caveat: DiaGem says the OGI numbers are somewhat off reality and elsewhere says Sarin/FacetWare scans were not accurate for this comparison; scanner values are context, not truth.

design_context.note: Stored only to distinguish intended/model values from the measured finished stone.

validation_contract.primary_task: Recover a 2D semantic Asscher wireframe/facet-family representation before attempting a full 3D physical reconstruction.
validation_contract.anti_leakage_rule: Specify and implement extraction without using the stored angle values as fitting targets.
expected_outputs: image-plane geometry explicitly separated from inferred physical geometry
checks: Compare image-derived P1/P2/P3/C1 estimates with Sergey's independent photo estimates after extraction.
Do not require perfect fourfold equality; the real stone contains known P3 and C3/table asymmetry.
Reject or strongly downweight images where pavilion side facets become visible from tilt/projection.
Do not infer physical P1/P2 length equality solely from apparent image-plane lengths.
non_goals: training a model on this single case
forcing exact agreement with Sergey or DiaGem by tuning thresholds
